limitations: v0 tracer is observe-only (declared => resident; no page.evict, no stub renders): no paging pressure at 253 (session-a) / 74 (session-b) declared tokens against the 200000 budget.

The derived-composition render tail is KNOWLEDGE-STATEFUL: a slice taken at turn N cannot prefix-extend a trace whose later turns declared new pages, and the full trace's final tail stamps earlier turns with post-hoc residency (253) that the mid-session package honestly shows as 93. diff(full, package) = shared pre-tail lifecycle prefix (10 events) + tallyMismatches turns 0-3 (253 vs 93); the design §3(3) shared-prefix evidence is carried by the CANONICAL pair instead — diff(era-as-flushed, package slice) = identical — precisely because the export chain is replay-deterministic. The m2 witness chain satisfied the naive full-vs-slice law only because m2-echo declares all pages by turn 2; m6 is the first drop to exercise a pause with later pages.

Resume is verify+provenance (design §3 v0): session-b re-reads its own state; page/turn identity transfer is possible in principle (pages are content-addressed) but trace injection (handoff-inject feature) is the gated v-next beat — this drop captures NO injection.
Session-b's resume evidence keeps the capture-time absolute snapshot path (corpus mapping documented in README); snapshotDigest links the shipped package bytes regardless.
tokenizerId is apx4-char (ceil(characters/4)) — approximation; absolute tokens are not provider usage. call.meta providerReported=false throughout (no provider cache counters surfaced).
The scripted beats run one-shot children (m2 pattern): hookStats context counts are the child runs' own model requests (session-a 7, session-b 3), not a long TUI session like m5.
